newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD still for EMU '99 but won't share power.
newsitem.headline: German SPD still for EMU '99 but won't share power.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats still want Europe's monetary union (EMU) to start in 1999 but would not join a grand coalition with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Wednesday.
Lafontaine told the Bild daily the SPD might have been ready last year to form a broad coalition with Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) to push through needed economic reforms.
But, he said, "this train has left the station."

Press reports said Kohl threatened to ditch his liberal Free Democratic (FDP) partners for a grand coalition if they did not agree to raising petrol taxes to fill gaps in the 1997 budget and qualify for EMU.
"Despite all the problems, I am in favour of launching the euro in 1999," Lafontaine said.
"The government has done everything to put up unnecessary hurdles. The overly tight interpretation of the Maastricht criteria has damaged the process of the monetary union."

Lafontaine said: "The Kohl government has reached the end of the road. If it goes on like this, it will gamble away the economic unification of Europe and Germany will slide further into unemployment."

Asked about a grand coalition, he said: "A government alliance of CDU and SPD was discussed a year ago. If the CDU had offered last year to agree to important reforms ... and really fight against unemployment, the SPD would have had to consider this alternative seriously. Now this train has left the station."
